elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms") and not every conditional preferred element is satisfied: the opt-out window is sixty (60) days rather than 30, and no Vendor renewal reminder is inserted. Because the automatic-renewal conditions are not all met, mutual written agreement would be required and is absent.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Retained language: "will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms" — each renewal term is 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted text requires "sixty (60) days' notice of non-renewal"; 60 days exceeds the 30-day preferred ceiling.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered 4(a)/(b); Kubient is not required to notify Customer in advance of any renewal.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Conditional does not apply: paragraph 4(a) renews the Agreement on unchanged terms and contains no unilateral uplift, indexation or re-pricing mechanic (fees/revenue share are fixed in each Exhibit), so no price-increase right is created on renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Renewal trigger now reads "will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless Customer gives sixty (60) days' notice of non-renewal or earlier terminated..." — a Customer non-renewal election at exactly the 60-day fallback ceiling, operating on the renewal itself rather than through the 90-day mutual termination right.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Conditional does not apply: the renewal provision confers no right to increase fees on renewal; the economics carry over unchanged from the Exhibits, so there is no uplift mechanic to cap.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the inserted Customer non-renewal election sits at the 60-day ceiling and no renewal price-increase mechanic exists to cap. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation, since the pre-edit clause gave Customer no way to stop renewal other than the 90-day mutual termination right (at the walk-away boundary).

Preferred level is not reached for two named defects the drafter would have to repair in operative language: (i) shorten the Customer opt-out from "sixty (60) days'" to "thirty (30) days'" notice; and (ii) add an express Kubient obligation to notify Customer at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date. These are noted, not required, because the fallback is satisfied.

Minimality holds: the change is a single inserted clause into the existing renewal trigger; nothing is deleted, and Kubient's 90-day post-Initial-Term termination right, its fee entitlement during the termination period, and the 4(b) breach/insolvency mechanics survive verbatim. No survival tails, procedures or extra requirements were added.

Intent preserved: non-renewal is distinct from termination, so the retained sentence "Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term" does not contradict a non-renewal notice given 60 days before the end of the Initial Term; no term is left undefined and no cross-reference dangles.

Drafting nits worth fixing without changing the outcome: anchor the window expressly ("sixty (60) days' notice of non-renewal prior to the end of the then-current term") so the temporal reference cannot be read as running from another date, and repair the grammar of "unless Customer gives sixty (60) days' notice of non-renewal or earlier terminated" (e.g. "...or is earlier terminated").
